headline: Israel debates unilateral strike on Iran while raising military readiness with US
body:
What happened: Israeli military readiness has risen amid concern that Iran could mount a surprise attack on Israel or US forces in the region. The IDF is coordinating closely with US Central Command, holding frequent calls and reinforcing command centres around the clock, with the Air Force under particular strain.

Inside Israel, reports say Mossad chief Roman Gofman favours a unilateral strike on Iran even without US participation, citing a suspected Iranian chemical weapons programme. Military chief Eyal Zamir backs eventual action but prefers waiting for US President Donald Trump and acting alongside Washington. The reporting says the US has not decided whether to strike, and that a window of about six weeks until the new Congress convenes was discussed; these accounts could not be independently verified.

Reported by: Jerusalem Post. Also covered by The New Arab, Asharq Al-Awsat, Xinhua, China Daily.

headline: Tribunal rejects Argentina's bid to halt Falklands oil project
body:
What happened: An international tribunal in Hamburg has declined Argentina's request to halt the Sea Lion oil project near the Falkland Islands. Judges voted 18 to 3 against Argentina's challenge, ruling that they lacked jurisdiction because they cannot decide questions of sovereignty over the islands. Argentina had sought a temporary order stopping drilling while its wider sovereignty claim went to arbitration.

The Sea Lion field, about 1.7 billion barrels, is being developed by Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum, with production planned for around 2028. The UK government said an order would have had serious consequences for islanders' right to develop their resources. Argentina's president Javier Milei has called the project illegal and imposed sanctions on firms involved.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by BBC News, The Guardian, Sky News, Al-Monitor.

headline: Kurds protest as Baghdad moves to take over oilfields and borders
body:
What happened: Thousands of Kurds protested in Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region on Thursday against Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's push to seize oilfields held by Kurdish security forces and station federal troops on the region's international borders. Iraq's highest court ruled Wednesday that Baghdad may deploy federal forces along all international borders, including in Kurdistan. The Kurdistan Regional Government rejected what it called military language and threats, though it said it would work with federal authorities against corruption and oil smuggling.

The moves follow a separate standoff in which Zaidi ordered the army to prepare to enter Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, where Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah is accused of smuggling; the group agreed to let soldiers in. Analysts warn that enforcing these measures against entrenched interests may prove difficult.

Reported by: France 24. Also covered by Al-Monitor, The New Arab, Arab News.

headline: Kyiv says Pyongyang paused some arms supplies to Moscow after diplomatic rift
body:
What happened: Ukraine's military intelligence agency said North Korea has temporarily suspended some military cooperation with Russia, including deliveries of KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery shells. The agency linked the pause to a dispute that began in October, after a Russian deputy foreign minister said the Kremlin would help ease tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang. North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui reportedly called such statements inconsistent with the alliance. The claims come from Ukraine and could not be independently verified.

Separately, Ukraine's energy sector has been hit hard by Russian strikes, with more than 1,000 attacks since September. Following a major attack on 20 November, Ukraine halted electricity exports entirely by 22 November, while imports rose sharply, mostly from Hungary.

Reported by: Sky News. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Independent.

headline: Italy says it was kept in the dark over Ukrainian strike in Libya
body:
What happened: Italy's foreign minister Antonio Tajani told parliament that Rome had no advance knowledge of a Ukrainian sea-drone attack on a Russian warship and a cargo vessel at the Libyan port of Benghazi. He said Italy opposed the decision and considers violating Libyan sovereignty a mistake, while still backing Kyiv. Libya's rival authorities condemned the strike, and Ukraine says its targets were Russian military assets and that it has no intention of extending the war to Libya.

Kyiv said the warship and cargo ship carried military equipment and were legitimate targets. Libya's eastern forces reported two naval personnel killed, and the Kremlin accused Ukraine of spreading the conflict into the Mediterranean.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, Africanews, Arab News, The New Arab.

headline: Kyiv Oblast faces emergency power cuts after Russian strikes and grid overload
body:
What happened: Authorities in Kyiv Oblast have introduced emergency electricity cuts after damage from Russian attacks and overloaded equipment, according to Ukraine's state grid operator Ukrenergo. Repair crews have started work, and the region will return to scheduled outages once the system allows. Separately, reporting indicates Ukraine halted electricity exports on November 22 after a Russian strike on its transmission network, while imports surged to their highest daily level since mid-June. Analysts at the Center for Economic Strategy say Russia has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on Ukraine's energy sector since September.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Reuters, Japan Times, Kyiv Independent.

headline: Russian strikes kill 10 and injure 55 across Ukraine in one day
body:
What happened: Russian attacks killed 10 people and wounded 55 across Ukraine over a single day, local authorities said. The deadliest incident was a strike on businesses in Nizhyn, Chernihiv Oblast, which killed seven and injured seven others on November 27. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 162 drones overnight on November 28, with most intercepted. Separately, Ukraine's president warned of a new mass strike being prepared, while Russia said it had struck drone-related sites in Kyiv.

The violence came amid wider escalation. Ukraine says its drones hit a Russian refinery and military airfield, and naval drones struck Russian vessels off Libya and in the Baltic. Power outages affected several Ukrainian regions after Russian attacks. US President Donald Trump said he had pressed Putin to scale back military action.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: EU leaders gather in Brussels for divided talks on budget and Ukraine aid
body:
What happened: EU leaders met in Brussels for a two-day summit focused on the bloc's next seven-year budget and a proposed 45 billion euro loan to Ukraine. European Council president António Costa offered a compromise budget that cuts 44 billion euros from an earlier plan, but diplomats expected no deal before the final summit of the year in December. Northern states favour a smaller budget focused on defence and competitiveness, while southern and eastern countries want to protect farming and poorer regions. Four states, Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, have resisted contributing to the Ukraine loan, prompting Germany to link the issues.

Reported by: Euronews. Also covered by AP, BBC News, DW, France 24.

headline: Drone swarm over RAF Lakenheath prompts US counter-drone response, Iran suspected
body:
What happened: The US military reportedly used counter-drone technology to repel around six drones that swarmed RAF Lakenheath, a British base used by the US Air Force, earlier in November. The Financial Times reported the drones were not recovered by British or American personnel and that Iran was suspected of links to the incident. The UK Ministry of Defence said police and US security forces responded on 13 November, the situation was quickly resolved, and normal security was restored. The White House and Pentagon did not immediately comment, and Tehran has denied involvement in similar incidents in Britain.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al-Monitor, Asharq Al-Awsat, CNA.

headline: Houthi drones target Saudi sites after coalition strikes Hodeidah port
body:
What happened: Saudi Arabia says its air defences intercepted several Houthi drones over its Eastern Province, including near the Ras Tanura oil terminal, with no casualties in the initial assessment. The Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's government had struck the rebel-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah, a key entry point for food and aid, and hit targets in Saada and Amran. The Houthis, who had earlier struck a tower in Riyadh and injured at least 11 people, threatened Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah and Yanbu. The coalition promised a firm response to attacks on civilian infrastructure.

Reported by: Middle East Eye. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Al Jazeera, Asharq Al-Awsat.

headline: Iranian strikes keep Gulf security under strain as Bahrain base stays thin
body:
What happened: A US naval base in Bahrain is still running with a small fraction of its pre-war staff after Iranian drone and missile strikes, according to a Washington Post report. The base was among the hardest hit US facilities, and nearby neighbourhoods, schools and businesses have largely emptied; damage is estimated at over $400 million. Separately, two Italian technicians working for Germany's Rheinmetall died in Kuwait after a drone strike that Italy and Kuwait blame on Iran. Tehran denies responsibility and calls the incident suspicious.

Italy's prime minister and the European Commission president condemned the Kuwait attack, with the EU calling for more pressure on Iran. Iran's attacks on Gulf states have continued despite US-Iran negotiations.

Reported by: Jerusalem Post. Also covered by Reuters, BBC News, Middle East Eye, Arab News.

headline: Israeli drone strike kills one man and wounds several in northern Gaza
body:
What happened: An Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the Bir al-Naaja area, west of the Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, on Friday evening, killing a Palestinian man identified as Khaled Assaf, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, citing witnesses. Several others were wounded, some seriously. Separately, a child was wounded by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis in the south.

The Palestinian health ministry said Israeli attacks killed at least 19 people and wounded 48 over the previous 48 hours. Officials say 1,705 Palestinians have been killed since the October ceasefire began, though the strikes have continued.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by AP, BBC News, Al Jazeera, The Guardian.

headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies including China, Beijing protests
body:
What happened: The United States has proposed additional tariffs on 14 trading partners, China among them, after a Section 301 investigation into alleged "overcapacity" in industries such as steel, electric cars and solar panels. China faces the highest rate, a 20 percent levy, with Washington threatening 40 percent if trade talks fail. Beijing's Commerce Ministry says it firmly opposes the measures, calls them unilateral and against WTO rules, and reserves the right to retaliate. It also urged Washington to implement a $30 billion reciprocal tariff reduction agreed in September.

Reported by: People's Daily. Also covered by Al Jazeera, China Daily.

headline: Russian convoy heading to Libya turns back after Benghazi warship sinking
body:
What happened: A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles to Libya has reportedly turned around in the Mediterranean, according to three people from military and security services who spoke to Reuters. The move followed an attack on November 22 at the Benghazi naval base, where a Russian corvette, the Merkury, was sunk. Libya's eastern-based government blamed a suspected drone attack, and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said the target was Russian; the convoy's diversion was not officially confirmed by Moscow, whose defence ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

The vessels were reportedly bound for Libya, with the cargo possibly intended for Russia's Africa Corps in West Africa or for forces loyal to Khalifa Haftar. The convoy was last tracked near Algeria, and its next destination remains unclear.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by France 24, Arab News, The Moscow Times, Japan Times.

headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly spark fire at Russian oil sites in Rostov and Bashkortostan
body:
What happened: Telegram monitoring channels reported that Ukrainian drones struck near the Novoshakhtinsk Oil Refinery in Russia's Rostov Oblast overnight on November 28, with a fire likely at fuel storage tanks, according to an OSINT analysis by the ASTRA channel. Kyiv could not immediately verify the reports, and Ukraine's military had not commented. The attack follows a strike on the same refinery on November 23 that reportedly destroyed or damaged dozens of storage tanks.

Separately, a drone crash sparked a fire at the Subkhankulovo oil pipeline control station, a major hub of Transneft's trunk pipeline system, in Bashkortostan. Local officials said no one was hurt and the extent of damage was unknown. Analysts estimate Russian refining volumes have fallen to their lowest level in over twenty years.

Reported by: Kyiv Independent. Also covered by Reuters, Ukrainska Pravda, The Moscow Times.

headline: Israeli strike in Gaza City fails to kill Hamas leader's son
body:
What happened: An Israeli air strike on a Gaza City residence hit the family of Izzeldeen al-Hayya, the last surviving son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya, but he and his family survived, Hamas said. Several relatives were reportedly wounded, including his daughter-in-law, though no deaths were reported. Hamas called the attack an attempt to assassinate him, linking it to threats from Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz, and said it undermined the October 2025 ceasefire.

The same day, other Israeli attacks in Gaza killed several Palestinians, according to local officials. Israel's military separately alleged that Hamas used part of Al-Ahli Baptist Hospital as an interrogation centre; Hamas rejected the claim and the hospital's diocese said it knew of no such site.

Reported by: Sky News. Also covered by Reuters, Al Jazeera, Asharq Al-Awsat, Middle East Eye.

headline: Trump endorses Iraqi premier's push to curb oil smuggling and central control
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's campaign against oil smuggling and his effort to bring armed groups under state control. Baghdad has moved to place Kurdistan's border crossings and several oil fields under federal authority, closing two crossings, one with Syria and one with Iran, and a court ruling allowed federal forces along all international borders. Kurdish officials rejected the federal moves as a violation of constitutional rights, though they say they do not want clashes. Iraq's oil minister says it will not tolerate exports outside legal channels. Analysts say the moves align with US pressure on Iran, which Iraqi and Kurdish sides both see as a major source of tension.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by The National, The New Arab, Arab News.

headline: Iranian drone debris kills two Italians at Kuwaiti site
body:
What happened: Two Italian nationals died after Iranian drones were intercepted over Kuwait, Kuwait's Defence Ministry said. The drones were aimed at a facility it called vital, and falling debris caused the deaths and damage. A Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national were also injured and taken to hospital. The Gulf Cooperation Council condemned the attack, backed Kuwait's right to defend itself, and held Tehran responsible.

The incident comes amid wider Gulf attacks, including Houthi missile and drone strikes on Saudi targets. Riyadh's coalition said a refinery at Jazan was hit and vowed a firm response.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by Reuters, France 24, The National, Al-Monitor.

headline: US strikes disables Palau-flagged cargo ship trying to leave Iran's Bandar Abbas
body:
What happened: US Central Command said a Palau-flagged commercial ship, the M/V Pacific Archer, was disabled in the Gulf of Oman on November 26 after its crew tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran. The ship had left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas, and US military aircraft fired precision munitions that hit its stern, disabling its propulsion. The civilian crew was not hurt, the military said.

The incident adds to US efforts to enforce the blockade of Iran, which the military says the vessel's crew was warned about before the strike.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by AP, Asharq Al-Awsat, Middle East Eye, Arab News.

headline: Iran's Guards say tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
body:
What happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps said several oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, near Oman's Khasab port. The Guards said the vessels were using unauthorised routes and had switched off tracking systems. One reported tanker was a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of crude and was left burning. The claims could not be independently verified.

The incidents come amid a US naval blockade of Iran. US Central Command separately said American aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored warnings to halt, and President Trump said no Iranian ship had passed the blockade.

Reported by: Fars. Also covered by Middle East Eye, Mehr News, Jerusalem Post.

headline: Reported Russian nuclear satellite raises fears of a space detonation
body:
What happened: German broadcasters and a newspaper, citing western intelligence assessments, report that Russia may launch a nuclear-enabled satellite called Sputnik-S within about 60 days. The satellite is said to have been assembled years ago and kept near Moscow. A German government spokesperson said the reports were being taken very seriously.

Experts explain that a nuclear blast in space releases energy as radiation rather than a mushroom cloud. In low Earth orbit, where most satellites operate, X-rays could disable spacecraft across thousands of miles, and trapped particles could last for years. Analysts recall the 1962 US Starfish Prime test, which damaged satellites and disrupted Hawaii.

Reported by: Arab News. Also covered by The Guardian, Asharq Al-Awsat, The Hindu.

headline: Kyiv's foreign minister urges Europe to act quickly on Ukraine funding
body:
What happened: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke at a joint press conference in Kyiv with Alain Berset, Secretary General of the Council of Europe. He argued that Ukraine's front line also defends European security, so backing Kyiv is a question of Europe's own protection. He warned that postponing decisions could later cost European states far more to defend their own territory.

Sybiha said Russia is trying to split Europe from the United States and to divide European Union members from one another, and called for united, collective responses. He also asked partners to weigh the case for Ukraine's macro-financial support, noting that Russia has raised its war budget and that Ukraine must match it proportionately.

Reported by: Ukrainska Pravda. Also covered by Reuters, Arab News.

headline: Reported Saudi strike in Yemen's Taiz kills civilians, unverified
body:
What happened: Houthi-affiliated media reported that Saudi air strikes killed 11 civilians, most of them children, in al-Turbah, south of Taiz city in Yemen. Rescuers reportedly recovered eight bodies, with three people still missing under rubble. Al Jazeera said it could not independently verify the claims, and the Saudi-led coalition did not immediately comment, though it later said it destroyed a Houthi drone aimed at Riyadh.

The reports come amid renewed fighting between Houthi forces and Saudi-backed government troops since July, which escalated as the US war on Iran intensified. The World Health Organization says over 13,000 people have been killed or injured since August, and aid groups warn of worsening hunger and displacement.

Reported by: The New Arab. Also covered by AP, Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye, Xinhua.

headline: Uganda plans to pull troops from Lubero as Kinshasa row deepens
body:
What happened: Uganda's army has said it will withdraw its forces from Lubero, a town in North Kivu province in eastern DR Congo, within about two weeks, handing security to Congolese troops. The move follows Kinshasa's summoning of Uganda's top diplomat over social media posts by Ugandan army chief Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, which included remarks about taking the mineral-rich town of Walikale. Uganda gave no reason for the withdrawal and did not say whether it was linked to the dispute. The army also accused militias, some apparently allied with Kinshasa, of attacking civilians.

Reported by: BBC News. Also covered by Africanews, France 24 Africa, Xinhua.

headline: Trump urges Putin to halt military action across Europe
body:
What happened: US President Donald Trump said he pressed Russian President Vladimir Putin during their recent meeting in China to end military aggression across European territories. He framed this as a way to help reach a quick deal between Russia and Ukraine, which he described as possible. The remarks follow Russian missiles and drones entering Polish airspace during strikes on Ukraine on November 23 and 24. Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte also called on Russia to avoid actions that could widen the war. The Kremlin, through spokesman Dmitry Peskov, placed blame on Ukraine for any escalation.

Reported by: France 24. Also covered by The Guardian, Le Monde, Kyiv Independent, Ukrainska Pravda.

headline: US drops business-deal incentives for Russia over Ukraine war, FT reports
body:
What happened: The Financial Times reports that the Trump administration has quietly set aside plans to offer Russia business deals in exchange for ending the war in Ukraine. The proposals covered energy and aviation ventures, including possible US investment in Russian oil projects and titanium production, plus a resumed pipeline gas supply to Europe. Officials told the paper the Kremlin showed little interest, and envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner now say territory and security are the focus. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

According to the sources cited, Moscow still insists on Ukrainian territorial concessions, which Kyiv rejects. The shift is described as a return to a "land for peace" approach.

Reported by: Al Jazeera. Also covered by France 24, Ukrainska Pravda, Meduza, The National.

headline: Sabotage against European infrastructure rises as Russia's hybrid campaign continues
body:
What happened: A report from the International Institute for Strategic Studies says Russia has stepped up unconventional tactics against European countries, including sabotage, reconnaissance and intimidation. Sabotage attacks on European infrastructure rose 16 percent in the year to September 2026, with arson and explosives use roughly doubling. Incidents include a drone attack on a German airport and attacks on energy sites and defence manufacturers.

The institute judges that the campaign has not deterred European support for Ukraine, as military aid has kept rising and European defence spending grew. Germany and Poland have been hit most, and the report expects them to remain main targets. Moscow rejects Western accusations that it is behind the campaign.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Al Jazeera, The Guardian, Kyiv Independent.

headline: EU summit ends without budget deal as states clash over spending and Ukraine aid
body:
What happened: EU leaders held a special summit in Brussels aimed at breaking a deadlock over the bloc's 2028 to 2034 budget, which is about 1.78 trillion euros in the compromise put forward by European Council President António Costa. Talks ended after midnight with no agreement, and a planned follow-up was set for 17 December. Frugal states including Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden want deeper cuts and more money for defence, while cohesion states want to protect spending on poorer regions and farming.

The summit also failed to settle a proposed loan of about 45 billion euros for Ukraine, which Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic oppose. Unanimity is required, and the deadline is pressured by national elections in several member states next year.

Reported by: Euronews. Also covered by Al Jazeera, France 24, Politico Europe, Le Monde.

headline: Unidentified drone briefly enters Latvian airspace, triggering alerts and jet response
body:
What happened: An unidentified drone briefly entered Latvian airspace in the early hours of Friday, according to the Latvian National Armed Forces. Air-raid style alerts were issued for Ludza Municipality, with an orange alert at 02:30, and a lower-level yellow alert for neighbouring Balvi Municipality. NATO Baltic Air Policing jets were scrambled, and Latvian forces launched an interceptor drone, which returned to base after the flight. Both alerts were lifted within about an hour.

The military warned that similar incursions could recur while Russia's war against Ukraine continues. The incident came as Ukrainian drones attacked Russia's Leningrad region, where the governor said more than 40 drones were downed. Poland had earlier accused Moscow of a similar border violation.

Reported by: Reuters. Also covered by Ukrainska Pravda, Daily Maverick, Euronews, The Hindu.
